applicant_utility.summary: Treat this record as a routing stub rather than a funding fact sheet: the official route for the Confucius Institute Scholarship runs through the platform at cis.chinese.cn, which today exposes only a login page with no published programme details, amounts or deadlines. The practical first step is to write to the Confucius Institute or Confucius Classroom nearest to you and ask three things: whether it holds scholarship allocations for the current cycle, what the current categories and amounts are, and when its internal nomination deadline falls. Do not budget against figures you find on aggregator sites - with the awarding body's public pages offline, amounts and windows can only be confirmed through your local Confucius Institute or the Confucius Institute administration itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants who already have a working relationship with a Confucius Institute or Confucius Classroom that receives scholarship allocations and can nominate them.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your local Confucius Institute or Confucius Classroom to confirm it holds allocations for the current cycle and to request the current category list, amounts and window
Ask which scholarship categories are open this cycle (language study, teaching Chinese to speakers of other languages and similar tracks usually have separate rules)
Confirm the current eligibility rules in writing with the institute, including age limits, nationality and Chinese-language requirements
Prepare notarised translations of diplomas and transcripts and a recent non-criminal record certificate, which Chinese-side scholarship applications of this kind routinely require
Keep HSK/HSKK evidence current if you are pursuing Chinese-language or Chinese-teaching tracks
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to a Chinese university instead of going through the Confucius Institute/Classroom route - the nomination step is the programme's structure
Applying through an institute without allocations, which produces no nomination regardless of merit
Waiting for the local nomination cycle to be announced before preparing documents, leaving too little time before the internal deadline
Relying on outdated figures copied from third-party listing sites
document_audit: Because public requirements are not currently published, have the local Confucius Institute confirm in writing which documents are mandatory this cycle
If a Chinese-language track applies, verify HSK/HSKK validity dates with the institute before applying
Keep notarised translations ready, since applications of this type are cross-language sensitive
alerts: The awarding body's public scholarship pages are currently unreachable (404): verify any detail you read elsewhere directly with your local Confucius Institute before acting on it

Allocations are distributed through Confucius Institutes and Classrooms, so availability is unevenly spread; absence of a local partner is itself an eligibility barrier
